Surgical Services

  • Surgical Services

Our skilled veterinarians offer a wide range of surgical services, from routine procedures to more advanced surgeries. title: Dentistry Services
html:
Dentistry Services

  • Home
  • Dentistry Services

Imagine the discomfort you’d feel if you never brushed your teeth or saw a dentist. For many dogs and cats, this is their painful reality. According to the American Veterinary Dental Society, over 80% of dogs and 70% of cats will experience dental disease by the age of 3. Dental (or periodontal) disease is the most commonly diagnosed health issue in pets.

Common signs of dental disease include:

  • Yellow or brown tartar buildup on the teeth
  • Red, swollen, or bleeding gums
  • Bad breath
  • Changes in eating or chewing habits
  • Pawing at the face
  • Loose teeth
  • Depression

Even if your pet doesn’t show these symptoms, we recommend having a veterinarian assess their dental health annually. Without proper care, bacteria and food particles can build up around the teeth, leading to deterioration of the surrounding soft tissue and bone. This can result in irreversible periodontal disease, tooth loss, and the need for costly oral surgery.

The first step is a comprehensive dental exam with your veterinarian. They will assess the condition of your pet’s teeth, determine whether a cleaning is necessary, and discuss the procedures required before the cleaning.

Dental disease doesn’t only affect the mouth—it can also impact other organs. Bacteria from the mouth can enter the bloodstream and lead to serious infections in the kidneys, liver, lungs, and heart. If left untreated, these infections can be fatal. A thorough exam, combined with appropriate lab tests, can help detect if the infection has spread.

Schedule your pet’s dental exam today! We can also guide you on how to brush your pet’s teeth and recommend foods and treats that help prevent plaque and tartar buildup.

We’re pleased to offer the following in-house services:

  • Dental Procedures
  • Tooth Extractions

title: Reference Laboratory Testing
html:
Reference Laboratory Testing

  • Home
  • Reference Laboratory Testing

Our team is proud to offer access to reference laboratory testing for cases that require advanced diagnostics.

While we provide a broad range of in-house diagnostic services, some situations may call for specialized testing to confirm a diagnosis, monitor therapeutic drug levels, or explore a systemic illness in more detail. For these advanced tests, samples are sent to trusted reference laboratories.

Using specialized laboratories offers the advantage of collaborating with highly trained internists and clinical pathologists who analyze the samples. These experts often work alongside our veterinarians to provide a deeper understanding of a patient’s condition, interpret results more thoroughly, and offer detailed treatment recommendations.

We offer access to a variety of reference laboratory tests, including:

  • Specialist diagnostic imaging interpretation
  • Pathology
  • Specialized blood testing
  • Urine Analysis
  • Fecal testing

For a complete list of available tests or to inquire about specific services, please contact our office. We’re here to ensure your pet gets the best possible care.

title: In-House Medical Imaging
html:
In-House Medical Imaging

  • Home
  • In-House Medical Imaging

Medical imaging offers a non-invasive way to gain valuable insights into your pet’s health. Our skilled team of imaging professionals is experienced in using advanced diagnostic equipment to support accurate and timely assessments.

We proudly offer a range of imaging techniques on-site for your convenience. 

Our in-house imaging services include:

  • Radiography (X-rays): X-rays provide detailed images of areas with contrasting tissue densities, making them ideal for evaluating bones, joints, and certain soft tissues.
  • Ultrasound: This imaging method uses sound waves to create real-time, two-dimensional images of internal organs, helping to assess the heart, abdomen, and reproductive system.
  • Electrocardiogram (ECG): This test measures the electrical activity of the heart, aiding in the diagnosis of heart rhythm abnormalities and other cardiac conditions.

Our goal is to provide accurate diagnostics in a comfortable, stress-free environment, helping ensure the best possible care for your pet.

title: In-House Laboratory Diagnostics
html:
In-House Laboratory Diagnostics

  • Home
  • In-House Laboratory Diagnostics

In-house laboratory services provide quick, reliable insights into your pet’s health—especially when a physical examination alone doesn’t reveal the full picture. These diagnostic tools help veterinarians make accurate assessments and start treatment without delay.

Having diagnostics performed on-site means you don’t have to wait for results to return from outside labs. In most cases, results are available within an hour, allowing for immediate action and timely care.

Laboratory testing is essential for the early detection of various health conditions such as liver and kidney disease, diabetes, urinary tract infections, parasitic infestations, and more. Early diagnosis often leads to better outcomes and faster recovery times.

A wide range of diagnostic tests are available in-house for your convenience. If a specific test isn’t available on-site, coordination with trusted reference laboratories ensures your pet receives the necessary care.

In-house diagnostic capabilities include:

  • Comprehensive Bloodwork
  • Urinalysis

If you have any questions or would like to book an appointment, don’t hesitate to contact us. The team is here to support you and your pet every step of the way.

title: Laser Surgery
html:
Laser Surgery

  • Home
  • Laser Surgery

As the demand for high-quality veterinary care grows, so does the importance of specialized services tailored to the needs of cats and dogs. These beloved companions require medical and surgical care that takes into account their unique anatomy, behavior, and health challenges.

Cats and dogs often show only subtle signs of illness, making early detection and prompt intervention essential. Veterinarians are trained to recognize species-specific behaviors, dietary needs, and environmental factors that impact overall well-being. Whether it’s managing chronic conditions like arthritis or kidney disease, treating allergies, or diagnosing internal issues, timely and accurate care can make a significant difference.

Surgical procedures for cats and dogs require expertise, precision, and careful attention to their specific needs. One advancement in veterinary surgery is the use of laser technology, which provides a less invasive alternative for many soft tissue procedures. Laser surgery can reduce pain, minimize bleeding, and promote quicker recovery—making it ideal for operations such as spaying, neutering, tumor removal, and dental surgery.

Preventive care—including routine checkups, vaccinations, parasite control, and proper nutrition—is key to ensuring a long, healthy life. When pet owners work closely with knowledgeable veterinarians, they can help their pets thrive through every stage of life.

With ongoing advancements in veterinary medicine—such as the adoption of laser surgery—pets today have access to more effective, comfortable, and compassionate care than ever before. By prioritizing their health needs, we support the well-being of the cats and dogs who are cherished members of our families

title: Wellness and Preventive Care
html:
Wellness and Preventive Care

  • Home
  • Wellness and Preventive Care

Taking a proactive approach to your pet’s health is one of the most loving things you can do. Preventive care lays the foundation for a long, happy life. With routine wellness exams, we can spot potential health concerns early and treat them before they become serious or life-threatening.

During a wellness visit, your veterinarian will conduct a thorough physical exam and discuss your pet’s diet, activity level, and overall well-being. Based on the exam and your pet’s health history, we’ll recommend tailored preventive care — which may include vaccinations, parasite prevention (against both external threats like fleas, ticks, and ear mites, and internal ones like worms and heartworm), dietary guidance, coat and skin maintenance, joint support, weight management, or dental care.

We proudly offer a full range of wellness and preventive services, including:

  • Comprehensive wellness exams
  • Vaccinations
  • Puppy and kitten wellness programs
  • Diabetic management
  • Flea and tick prevention
  • Nutritional counselling
  • Travel certificates and documentation
  • Medical grooming
  • Spay and neuter surgeries
  • Professional dental cleaning and extractions

About Us

Since opening its doors in 2010, Dundas East Animal Hospital has been dedicated to delivering high-quality veterinary care to pets in the Mississauga community. With a focus on compassionate service and personalized treatment, the hospital has earned a trusted reputation among pet owners seeking reliable and professional care.

The experienced veterinary team at Dundas East Animal Hospital offers a full range of services, from preventive health check-ups and vaccinations to surgical procedures and diagnostics. Their approach emphasizes early detection and effective treatment, helping pets lead longer, healthier lives. Equipped with modern technology and a well-trained staff, the hospital is committed to maintaining the highest standards in veterinary medicine.

What sets Dundas East Animal Hospital apart is its client-centered philosophy. The staff understand the important role pets play in the lives of their owners, and they strive to create a welcoming, stress-free environment for both animals and their humans. They take time to communicate clearly, answer questions, and involve pet owners in every step of their pet’s care.

Over the years, the hospital has built strong relationships with the community through its dedication to honest advice, expert care, and a genuine love for animals. Whether it’s a routine visit or a complex medical concern, the team ensures each pet is treated with respect, kindness, and professionalism.

Dundas East Animal Hospital remains a reliable partner in pet health, proudly serving families and their furry companions with warmth and integrity for over a decade.

title: How weather changes affect your pet’s health
html:
Pets are susceptible to weather variations, just like people, and these variations may have a greater effect on their behaviour and general health than you may think. Understanding how the seasons impact your pet can help you keep them content and healthy all year long, from seasonal allergies to cold-weather discomfort.
In Warmer Weather: Heatstroke can be brought on by rising temperatures, particularly in dogs with flat faces like pugs or bulldogs. Always offer water and shade, and keep an eye out for signs of weakness, drooling, or excessive panting. If the pavement is too hot for your palm, it will be too hot for their paws, which might cause them to burn sensitive paw pads.

Allergies that manifest as itching, red skin, or ear infections are also common in the spring and summer. Current prophylactic measures are essential because warm weather is ideal for fleas, ticks, and mosquitoes.
In colder climates, pets—particularly those with short hair—can become quite cold very quickly. During severe cold spells, restrict your time outside and think about pet sweaters because hypothermia and frostbite are serious concerns. Cooler temperatures can also make older pets and those with arthritis feel more rigid or achy.

Dry winter air can cause damaged paws and sensitive skin. After walks, rub your pet off with pet-safe moisturisers to get rid of chemicals that cause salt or ice melt.
We at [Dundas East Animal Hospital] are available to help you navigate every season. Don’t be afraid to contact us if you observe any changes in your pet’s behaviour or health; we can assist you in determining the cause, even if it’s weather-related.

title: Pet allergies: symptoms, causes, and treatments
html:
Not only may allergies affect people, but they can also affect our pets. Pet allergies may be both upsetting and frustrating for both pets and their owners, whether they manifest as itchy skin, watery eyes, or persistent ear infections. The good news? Allergies can be efficiently treated with the right diagnosis and treatment.

Common Symptoms of Pet Allergies:

  • Persistent scratching, licking, or biting
  • Red, inflamed, or flaky skin
  • Hair loss or hot spots
  • Chronic ear infections
  • Watery eyes or sneezing
  • Digestive issues like vomiting or diarrhoea (in food allergies)

What Leads to Allergies in Pets?

Pet allergies typically fall into one of three categories:
Atopy, or environmental allergies, can be brought on by dust mites, mould, pollen, and even grass. Although they can happen all year round, these are frequently seasonal.

1. Food Allergies: Dairy, wheat, beef, and chicken are common causes. Usually, food allergies manifest as gastrointestinal distress or skin problems.
2. Flea Allergy Dermatitis: A single flea bite can result in severe skin inflammation and itching in certain pets that are very sensitive to flea saliva.

Options for Treatment:
Finding the trigger is the first step in managing pet allergies. Your veterinarian can suggest flea management, an elimination diet, or allergy testing. Treatment options could consist of:

  • Antihistamines or corticosteroids
  • Prescription allergy medications or immunotherapy
  • Medicated shampoos and skin supplements
  • Specialized diets

We at [Dundas East Animal Hospital] are aware of the impact allergies can have on your pet’s well-being. Our staff is here to assist you in identifying the cause and developing a customised treatment strategy that provides long-lasting alleviation.

title: Understanding common skin conditions in pets
html:
Pets frequently visit the veterinarian for skin problems, and with good cause. The largest organ in your pet and a major sign of general health is their skin. If left untreated, an abnormality can lead to discomfort, tension, and possibly major problems.
1. One of the main causes of inflamed, itchy skin is allergies. Certain foods, fleas, pollen, and even dust mites can cause allergies in pets. Excessive licking, scratching, or red, swollen skin are symptoms. Finding the allergen and controlling it with medication, dietary modifications, or environmental changes might provide much-needed relief.
2. Infestations of fleas are another major offender. Sensitive pets may experience significant reactions after just one flea bite. It’s crucial to regularly prevent fleas, particularly in the summer months.

3. Scratching or licking can quickly result in the development of hot spots, which are raw, moist patches of skin. In order to stop infection and encourage healing, these require immediate care.
4. Both humans and pets can contract infectious fungal illnesses like ringworm. Common symptoms include red circular sores, scaly areas, and hair loss. Stopping the spread requires accurate diagnosis and treatment.
5. A bad diet, harsh shampoos, or environmental factors like dry air can all contribute to dry skin and dandruff. To restore the health of your skin, your veterinarian may suggest adjustments or supplements.

Don’t wait if you observe your pet scratching more than normal or if their skin or coat changes. Our goal at [Dundas East Animal Hospital] is to identify, care for, and ensure that your pet is literally at ease in their own skin.

title: Spay or neuter? what every pet owner should consider
html:
One of the most crucial choices you can make as a good pet owner is whether to spay or neuter your animal companion. This easy process has several behavioural and health advantages that can help your pet live a longer, happier life in addition to avoiding unwanted litters.
The risk of some diseases and malignancies can be considerably decreased by spaying (for females) and neutering (for males). Neutered male pets are protected against testicular cancer and certain prostate problems, while female pets are less prone to develop breast tumours and uterine infections. Furthermore, sterilised pets are frequently calmer and less prone to wander, mark their territory, or act aggressively.

Spaying and neutering contributes to the fight against pet overpopulation from a community perspective. Millions of dogs and cats wind up in shelters every year, and many are put down because there isn’t enough room or funding. Your decision to sterilise your pet is part of a bigger solution.
The idea that pets should only have one litter or go through a heat cycle before being spayed is also a prevalent misconception. In actuality, early spaying and neutering—typically between the ages of 4 and 6 months—is advantageous and safe.

We at [Dundas East Animal Hospital] are committed to assisting pet owners in making the best decisions for their animals by educating them. Our kind staff is available to answer any questions you may have regarding the process, the schedule, or the aftercare.

The health of your pet and the animal population as a whole will be greatly impacted by spaying or neutering.

title: The ultimate guide to puppy and kitten care
html:
The pleasure of bringing a new puppy or kitten into your house is thrilling and endearing, but it also carries a lot of responsibility. The basis for a happy, healthy future is laid during the first few months of life.
1. Veterinary Care: Make an appointment for your initial visit as soon as you can. Beginning at 6 to 8 weeks of age, puppies and kittens require a course of vaccines, deworming, and flea prevention. Along with discussing when to spay or neuter, your veterinarian will also look for congenital problems.

  1. Nutrition: A food especially designed for growth is necessary for young pets. Select premium puppy or kitten food and adhere to age- and breed-size-appropriate feeding recommendations. There should always be access to fresh water.
  2. Socialisation and Training: Get your puppy or kitten out there as soon as possible. Gently and constructively introduce them to other people, sounds, and settings. Start house or litter training and basic training immediately. For both pups and kittens, positive reinforcement is the most effective method.
  3. Grooming & Hygiene: To minimise shedding and help your pet become accustomed to grooming, brush them frequently. While kittens usually groom themselves but benefit from brushing and nail care, puppies require nail trims and sometimes baths.
  4. Safety: Make your house pet-proof. Keep tiny things, cables, and poisonous plants out of reach. To help them feel comfortable, give them safe toys and a special place to sleep.

 

We at [Dundas East Animal Hospital] are here to help you at every turn with your new pet. Give them the finest start in life by scheduling their initial examination right now!

title: Why annual vet checkups can save your pet’s life
html:
You want your pet to have a long, happy, and healthy life because you are a pet parent. Making an appointment for yearly veterinarian examinations is one of the best ways to guarantee that. These visits have the potential to save lives, so they are more than just regular.
Because they mature far more quickly than people, pets may experience rapid changes in their health. Your veterinarian can identify early symptoms of illness that might not be apparent at home with an annual visit. Cancer, diabetes, kidney disease, and arthritis are among the conditions that frequently begin quietly. Many of these problems can be successfully treated with early discovery, enhancing your pet’s quality of life and possibly extending their lifespan.

Your veterinarian will conduct a wellness exam, which includes a complete physical examination, vital sign and weight checks, immunisation updates, and sometimes blood or urine testing. These tests aid in determining any underlying problems and creating a baseline of health for later use.
Exams are also the ideal time to talk about your pet’s food, behaviour, dental health, and any changes you’ve noticed. Weight management, dental cleanings, and parasite control are examples of preventive care that can keep minor problems from developing into major health difficulties.

At [Dundas East Animal Hospital], we think that the best way to maintain your pet’s health is to provide preventative care. Even when your pet appears to be doing well, yearly visits guarantee they get the care they need.
Schedule your pet’s yearly wellness examination now to give them the best chance at living a long, active life. It’s worth it for your furry family member!

title: Vaccinations for pets: what every pet parent must know
html:
Maintaining the health of your beloved friend is a primary concern for any devoted pet owner. Vaccinations are among the most crucial preventive care measures. Pets are protected by vaccines against a wide range of infectious and possibly fatal illnesses, many of which are incurable.
Vaccines against rabies, distemper, parvovirus, and adenovirus are essential for dogs. Vaccines against calicivirus, herpesvirus, feline distemper (panleukopenia), and rabies are commonly administered to cats. Other non-core vaccinations, such as Bordetella or feline leukaemia, might also be suggested based on your pet’s lifestyle.

By halting the transmission of disease, vaccinations not only protect your pet but also the larger community. At 6 to 8 weeks of age, puppies and kittens start their vaccination series, which is followed by booster doses. Depending on the immunisation, adult pets require updates on a regular basis, usually once a year or every three years.
To create a customised immunisation plan depending on your pet’s age, health, and lifestyle, always speak with your veterinarian. We at [Dundas East Animal Hospital] are available to help you at every stage of your pet’s medical journey.

One easy method to ensure your pet has a long, happy, and healthy life is to keep up with immunisations. Make an appointment for your pet’s upcoming health checkup now!

Prevention is vital; don’t wait until illness strikes. Vaccines are safe, effective, and essential for responsible pet ownership. Protect your best friend and give them the healthiest life possible.

title: 10 signs your pet needs to see a vet — don’t ignore them
html:
It is up to us to recognise the warning signs because our dogs are unable to communicate with us when something is amiss. Early detection of health issues can be greatly aided by observing even little changes in behaviour, appetite, or energy levels. These are ten indicators that your pet might require medical attention.
1. A shift in thirst or appetite may be a sign of diabetes, kidney illness, dental problems, or other health conditions. It’s important to pay attention to eating or drinking much more or less than normal.
2. A discernible decrease in energy or lethargy could indicate an infection, discomfort, or another underlying illness. It’s time for a checkup if your pet appears disinterested in activities or is napping more than normal.
3. Prolonged diarrhoea or vomiting, particularly when accompanied by blood or tiredness, can indicate serious internal or digestive problems.
4. Thyroid issues, parasites, or chronic diseases may be the cause of unexplained weight loss or increase that does not correspond with dietary or activity changes.
5. Breathing difficulties, especially laboured or fast breathing, are dangerous symptoms that may be related to heart or respiratory issues.
6. If your pet has a chronic cough or sneeze, you should see a veterinarian because these symptoms may be caused by allergies, infections, or irritants.
7. Limping, stiffness, or trouble moving might be signs of joint illnesses, arthritis, or traumas; if addressed, these symptoms could worsen.
8. Excessive biting, scratching, or hair loss may indicate parasite infestations, skin illnesses, or allergies.
9. Urinary or gastrointestinal problems may be indicated by changes in urine or defecation, such as accidents, straining, or visible blood.
10. Your pet may exhibit unusual behaviour as a means of expressing pain or discomfort, such as increased aggression, hiding, or restlessness.

Don’t wait if your pet exhibits any of these symptoms. Minor concerns can be avoided from becoming major ones with prompt veterinary care.
